speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Given your history of AIDS and symptoms of decreased vision and black spots in your right eye, I need to determine if this is an opportunistic infection. Have you noticed any floaters, flashes of light, or a curtain-like shadow over your vision? REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mention of a prior TB diagnosis is concerning, but the specific ocular symptoms of black spots and decreased vision in an AIDS patient strongly suggest Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis. Have you experienced any recent flu-like symptoms, fever, or mouth sores? REQUEST TEST: CMV_DNA_PCR. REQUEST IMAGES: Fundoscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CMV_DNA_PCR: Positive; Fundoscopy: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV Retinitis. The positive CMV DNA PCR and the fundoscopy findings of granular yellow-white opacities with dot-blot hemorrhages in your right eye, combined with your AIDS history, confirm the diagnosis.
